To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new transgenic mouse model for tracing the gustatory and the trigemino-solitary chemosensory neural pathways originating from the taste receptor cells and nasal solitary chemoreceptor cell.
we established transgenic mice to trace the gustatory and chemosensory neural pathways from T1R-expressing taste cells and solitary chemosensory cells, respectively.
we developed the first transgenic mouse model for tracing gustatory and trigeminally innervated solitary chemoreceptor neural pathways from T1R-expressing taste cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic tracing of the gustation and chemoreception.
the molecular genetic basis of the gustatory neural pathways and the neural circuits of the solitary chemoreceptor neurons in the nasal cavity.
the genetic and functional organization of the gustatory pathways in the mouse.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the T1R3 protein is a reliable marker of sweet/umami receptor cells, but is not a specific marker for the sweet/umani taste pathway.
T1R3 is expressed in taste receptor cells, solitary chemoreceptor, and some neurons in the brain stem.
T1R3 is a marker for the sweet/umamigustatory pathway and solitary chemosensory pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the t1r-WGA transgenic mouse is a unique tool to visualize gustatory pathways originating from taste receptor cells, which are the only known chemosensory cells in the taste system, and to visualize the trigeminal pathways originating from solitary chemoreceptors, the only known chemoreceptor cells outside the tongue.

the T1R3 receptor protein is not only expressed in sweet and umami taste receptor cells but also expressed in a subset of solitary chemoreceptor cell neurons in the nasal cavity, and that the T1r3-WG mice can be a valuable tool to investigate the neural circuits of the taste and trigeminal pathways.
T1R3 is not only a receptor for sweet/umami but also an indispensable molecular marker for the sweet/umamigenic gustatory and the trigeminochemical pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the t1r 3-WGA transgenics provide a new and powerful tool to investigate the gustatory and the trigemino-nasal neural pathways.
the T1R3-WGA transgene faithfully labels the gustatory and solitary chemoreceptive neural pathways from the taste and solitary chemoreceptors.
the t1r 3 -WGA transgenic mouse is a powerful tool for tracing gustatory and chemosensory pathways from the taste buds and solitary chemoreceptors, respectively.
